title: Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards (Registration Fees) Bill 2013
portfolio: Sustainability, Environment, Water, Population and Communities

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Introduced the Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards Registration Fees Bill, giving the WELS scheme a legal basis to recover the 80 per cent of costs through registration fees it was intended to achieve when established in 2005 but never reached.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Introduced the Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards Amendment Registration Fees Bill, making consequential changes to allow proper collection and administration of the new registration fees introduced by the companion bill.

speeches.speaker: Greg Combet
speeches.brief: Moved to refer the Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards (Registration Fees) Bill and its amendment bill to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Supported the WELS registration fees bills, arguing that labelling helps consumers choose efficient products and could save about 100,000 megalitres of domestic water use each year by 2025, 800,000 megalitres nationally and about 400,000 tonnes of greenhouse gas emissions each year. Said compliance should protect the system's integrity while being applied with common sense.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Argued that the bills would allow WELS fees to recover 80 per cent of scheme costs, representing around $1.7 million per annum, while warning that ministerial fee-setting could become an unaccountable tax or levy. Supported the scheme but backed a Senate inquiry into efficiency, cost and compliance.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Reported that the WELS registration fees bills provide for the scheme's long-term viability and supported the scheme's contribution to water efficiency in Australia. Commended the bills to the House.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: The Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards (Registration Fees) Bill 2013 is a housekeeping bill to correct the labelling system for shower heads, and the speaker commended it to the Senate.

speeches.speaker: Kate Lundy
speeches.brief: The speaker tabled an addendum to the explanatory memorandum for the Export Finance and Insurance Corporation Amendment Bill 2013 and an additional statement on water efficiency legislation, and announced the government will review financial participants in the scheme and develop options for wider participation.

acts.title: Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards (Registration Fees) Act 2013
